conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that based on high-quality scientific evidence, ivermectin does not lower the risk of death in COVID-19 patients, directly rejecting the claim.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion**  
Based on high-quality scientific evidence, **ivermectin does not lower the risk of death** in COVID-19 patients.

**Key Evidence**
* **Systematic Reviews:** A comprehensive review by the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews analyzed multiple randomized controlled trials and found no evidence that ivermectin reduces all-cause mortality, prevents clinical deterioration, or speeds up recovery in outpatients or hospitalized COVID-19 patients (https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD015017.pub3/abstract).
* **Randomized Clinical Trials:** The TOGETHER trial, a large randomized placebo-controlled study published in *The New England Journal of Medicine*, found that early treatment with ivermectin did not result in a lower risk of hospitalization, emergency care visits, or mortality compared to placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).
* **Global Health Recommendations:** The World Health Organization (WHO) advises that ivermectin should not be used to treat or prevent COVID-19 outside of clinical trials due to a lack of demonstrated clinical efficacy regarding mortality and other key endpoints (https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/who-advises-that-ivermectin-only-be-used-to-treat-covid-19-within-clinical-trials).

In summary, rigorous clinical data show that ivermectin is ineffective at reducing mortality or preventing severe outcomes from COVID-19.
